payload.summary: No InferenceX checkout (INFERENCEX_PATH unset) and pr_monitor disabled, so scout ran on source + baseline-log archaeology. Read model config.json (Qwen3.5 hybrid GDN: 48/64 linear-attn layers, fp32 recurrent state), the installed vLLM 0.28.0+rocm723 flag surface, and the 1.5MB baseline server.log. Decomposed the 512.5 tok/s baseline: prefill and decode are ~fully serialized (~29% of wall clock is prefill at 27-278 gen tok/s), and decode's dominant HBM traffic is the 72MB/request fp32 GDN state working set. Three source-backed levers; no patch, no benchmark.

proposal_set.name: gdn-ssm-state-bf16
proposal_set.reason: config.json declares text_config.mamba_ssm_dtype='float32' and vLLM's Qwen3_5ForConditionalGenerationConfig.verify_and_update_config copies that straight into cache_config.mamba_ssm_cache_dtype when it is 'auto' (model_executor/models/config.py:781-805). So the GDN recurrent state cache is fp32. Per request per decode step the 48 linear-attn layers read+write a [48 v-heads,128k,128v] state = 786KB/layer, ~37.8MB read + ~37.8MB write = ~75MB of HBM traffic, vs ~12MB of KV for the 16 full-attn layers at seq 2k. At conc=64 that is ~4.8GB/step against ~3.9TB/s peak (~1.2ms of pure state movement per ~28ms step, 10-20% of the decode step) and it scales with concurrency while GEMM time does not. bf16 halves the state bytes; INT8 W8A8 already halves the weight-side traffic, so state bandwidth is proportionally MORE dominant here than in a bf16 run. Baseline steady-state decode is 729 tok/s vs 512.5 reported, so decode-side wins translate almost 1:1. Secondary effect confirmed in the log: 'Setting attention block size to 784 tokens to ensure that attention page size is >= mamba page size' - the 784-token attention block is derived from the mamba page, so halving the state shrinks that forced page inflation and the associated fragmentation.
source_evidence: /opt/envs/vllm/lib/python3.12/site-packages/vllm/config/cache.py:38,133 (MambaDType literal includes bfloat16; --mamba-ssm-cache-dtype registered at engine/arg_utils.py:1237)
runs/baseline/51ac28ff8aed4ad59746fdb889fae7bb/benchmark_vllm_20260915_103510/server.log 10:36:48 (attention block size 784 derived from mamba page size)
kb_evidence: model_arch.json: kv_cache_per_token small; block_size forced to ~848 tokens by mamba/GDN page alignment
model_arch.json law 10: 27B INT8 single-die hits ~80 tok/s single-stream WITH dflash, ~50-65 without

proposal_set.name: decoder-for-triton-attn-backend
proposal_set.reason: The selector logged 'Found incompatible backend(s) [TURBOQUANT] with AttentionType.DECODER. Overriding with ROCM_ATTN out of potential backends: [ROCM_ATTN, TRITON_ATTN]' - so ROCM_ATTN was picked by elimination, not by preference, and TRITON_ATTN is the other already-validated-compatible candidate. ROCM_ATTN implements prefill+decode in one fused Triton kernel, and its own module logged 'Cannot use ROCm custom paged attention kernel, falling back to Triton implementation' (chunked_prefill_paged_decode.py:463) - the plain chunked-prefill-paged-decode path, which is markedly weaker than a flash-style split prefill kernel at hd=256 / 24Q-4KV heads. That matters a lot here: from the baseline log, prefill windows run 1252-1843 prompt tok/s while generation in the SAME window collapses to 27-278 tok/s, i.e. prefill and decode are essentially serialized; ~38.5s of prefill per 133s wave (~29% of wall clock) is spent on a kernel that fell back. head_dim=256 is inside ROCM_ATTN's and TRITON_ATTN's supported head sizes, so this is a like-for-like backend swap with no shape risk. Not the AITER FA path that platform law 11 rules out for hd256 - that would need VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MHA/UNIFIED_ATTENTION and is explicitly a known dead end; this proposal does not touch it.
source_evidence: runs/baseline/51ac28ff8aed4ad59746fdb889fae7bb/benchmark_vllm_20260915_103510/server.log (rocm.py:703 backend override to ROCM_ATTN; chunked_prefill_paged_decode.py:463 ROCm custom paged-attn fallback)
kb_evidence: model_arch.json law 11: AITER fmha_v3 ASM covers hd128/192 only - do NOT propose ROCM_AITER_FA for this decoder

proposal_set.name: prefill-batch-4096
proposal_set.reason: max_num_batched_tokens is not set in the base recipe, so it is the SchedulerConfig.DEFAULT_MAX_NUM_BATCHED_TOKENS = 2048 (config/scheduler.py:42,49). Output throughput is bounded by wall clock, and prefill is ~29% of it (327680 input tokens at ~1700-1843 tok/s peak = ~38.5s per 5-wave cycle vs ~94.5s of decode at the 92.3ms median ITL). Raising the per-step token budget to 4096 lets 3-4 1024-token prefills share one step instead of ~2, which on CDNA2 lifts the attention/GEMM shapes out of the skinny regime and amortises the per-step fixed cost (64 GDN state reads/writes + graph replay) that is otherwise paid once per prefill chunk. Cheapest-to-interpret complement to the two kernel-side proposals: it attacks prefill throughput directly rather than decode. Note the current compile range endpoint is 2048, so this adds a second dynamo compile range (longer warmup, covered by the existing compile cache); if the run shows TPOT mean degrading while TTFT improves, revert.

new_findings.what: Baseline 512.5 tok/s decomposes as ~729 tok/s steady-state decode (all-zero-prompt-throughput windows) vs ~27-278 tok/s generation during prefill windows: prefill and decode are almost fully serialized. Accounting: 5 waves x (38.5s prefill + 94.5s decode) = 665s vs the measured 639.3s duration. ~29% of wall clock buys zero output tokens, so prefill-side and decode-overlap levers are worth roughly the same as decode-speed levers on this workload.
new_findings.expected_impact: frames the whole remaining headroom: 512.5 -> 729 tok/s is +42%

new_findings.what: Capacity is NOT the binding constraint: GPU KV cache usage peaks at 57.3% and 'Waiting: 0 reqs' for most of the run, and the engine reports Prefix cache hit rate 38-76%. num_gpu_blocks is therefore over-provisioned for conc=64, so gpu-memory-utilization and KV-capacity tuning are dead ends on this workload - do not spend proposal slots on them.

GDN recurrent state is fp32 because the checkpoint declares mamba_ssm_dtype='float32' and vLLM auto-adopts it, not because a kernel requires fp32. The state cache is the single largest per-step HBM traffic source at conc=64 (~75MB per request per decode step over 48 linear-attn layers) and the 784-token attention block size is inflated specifically to match that mamba page size. --mamba-ssm-cache-dtype is a first-class CLI flag in 0.28.0+rocm723 and accepts bfloat16/float16.
new_findings.expected_impact: 3-10% output tok/s; unblocks further page-size gains
new_findings.accuracy_risk: moderate: deviates from the vendor-declared fp32 state precision on a W8A8 checkpoint whose accuracy headroom is already thin (baseline 0.9674). The delta-rule recurrence may still accumulate in fp32 and only narrow the store, in which case the loss is sub-1-ulp per step, but it has not been measured here - recommend the accuracy gate run at a tightened floor before KEEP.

new_findings.what: The decoder attention backend was selected by elimination, not merit: ROCM_ATTN was used only because TURBOQUANT was rejected for AttentionType.DECODER, and ROCM_ATTN itself logged a fallback to the Triton chunked_prefill_paged_decode kernel. TRITON_ATTN is the other candidate the selector deemed compatible, and head_dim=256 is within ROCM_ATTN's supported head sizes [32,64,80,96,128,160,192,224,256]. This is distinct from the AITER fmha_v3 ASM path that platform law 11 rules out for hd256.

MTP is NOT a dead end for framework support but IS unjudgeable on this benchmark: the checkpoint ships 15 usable 'mtp.*' weights (bf16, listed in quantization_config.ignore), 'qwen3_5_mtp' is a registered MTPModelTypes value, and speculative.py:551-572 auto-derives n_predict from text_config.mtp_num_hidden_layers=1 with architecture Qwen3_5MTP. This directly contradicts the model_arch.json note 'mtp: not built into 0.28.0+rocm723 here' - the model file qwen3_5_mtp.py exists and is in the registry. The reason it is NOT in proposal_set is platform law 8: the sealed corpus is random-token (RANDOM_RANGE_RATIO=1), which collapses draft acceptance, so a measured number here cannot credit or discredit it.
new_findings.expected_impact: potentially large on natural prose, unmeasurable here
new_findings.accuracy_risk: none if acceptance-correct sampling; lossless by construction

new_findings.what: Environment/tooling gaps for this round: INFERENCEX_PATH is unset and state.json active_inferencex_path is empty, so reference launch scripts (source 1) were unreachable; pr_monitor is disabled (pr_degraded_reason ir3_auto), so source 3 upstream PR survey was unavailable. Findings are therefore 100% from model config.json + installed-source inspection + baseline run artifacts. Note also AITER_LOG_TUNED_CONFIG=1 is set in the base env but is pure log noise given law 5.

Warm-start recipe is seed_only with confidence 0.0 and hardware 'unknown_gpu', best_throughput 0.0, and empty lessons/pitfalls/what_worked - no prior validated config exists for this canonical_id, so nothing here was derived from a RecipeKB win. Real hardware is gfx90a (manifest.json gfx_arch), i.e. the recipe's hardware field is mislabelled and should be corrected on writeback.

Base launch args leave the multimodal stack loaded in a wasteful configuration: --language-model-only IS present (good), but VLLM_EXECUTE_MODEL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=1200 and CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES deprecation warnings ('support will be removed in vLLM v0.26.0. Please use HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES instead', rocm.py:134, emitted twice from APIServer and EngineCore) are logged every launch. Cosmetic, but the HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES migration is a real forward-compat item if the image is ever bumped.

Three Triton kernels JIT-compiled DURING the measured inference window (jit_monitor.py:141: _fwd_kernel, batch_memcpy_kernel, fused_sigmoid_gating_delta_rule_update_kernel) and the log's own advice is 'consider extending warmup to cover this shape/config'. NUM_WARMUPS=8 with 320 prompts; the first measured window (10:37:34) shows 239.9 gen tok/s, consistent with cold-shape compilation being charged to the measurement. fused_sigmoid_gating_delta_rule_update_kernel is a GDN decode kernel, so its cold compile lands on the decode path itself.

residual_questions: Is the GDN decode kernel (fused_recurrent_gated_delta_rule_packed_decode / fused_sigmoid_gating_delta_rule_update in model_executor/layers/mamba/gdn/qwen_gdn_linear_attn.py) able to consume a bf16 recurrent state directly, or does it assert/quietly fall back? Needs a one-line source read or a launch-log check, not a benchmark.

What actually causes generation to collapse to 27 tok/s during prefill windows on a hybrid GDN model - scheduler admission policy under mamba_cache_mode='align', the 784-token page granularity, or the chunked_prefill_paged_decode fallback kernel? A roofline snapshot over a prefill window would separate compute-bound from launch-bound.

Does --long-prefill-token-threshold interact safely with mamba cache 'align' mode, where cached states only land at multiples of mamba_block_size (= block_size = 784)? Sub-784 thresholds would never hit a chunk boundary and could silently destroy mamba prefix-cache reuse - needs source confirmation before anyone proposes it.

What is the accuracy gate tolerance relative to baseline 0.9674 on this W8A8 checkpoint? Both the bf16-state proposal's acceptability and any future quantized-KV idea hinge on that margin, and it is not in the advisory context.

Can a future scout round get an INFERENCEX checkout (INFERENCEX_PATH is unset) and pr_monitor enabled, so reference launch scripts and upstream Qwen3.5/GDN PRs become surveyable instead of relying on local-source archaeology?

Should the model_arch.json note 'mtp: not built into 0.28.0+rocm723 here' be corrected to 'present in registry but unmeasurable on random-token corpora', so the next framework round does not skip it for the wrong reason?

Does VLLM_ROCM_SHUFFLE_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT (default False in envs.py) change the paged-KV layout in a way that benefits hd256/GQA-4KV decode reads on gfx90a? Untested and outside the platform laws, so not proposed this round.
